name: speckit-xref
description: Keeps a GitHub Spec Kit feature and its code tied together inside Claude Code: a new idea researched and shaped with you, the spec in the system prompt, every edit booked against a task, a proof ladder per requirement, a local dashboard, and an autopilot gated by your decisions and the tests.

mode.title: Drift mode
mode.description: advisory: the mod tells the model and the person about drift. strict: it also refuses edits outside the current task's planned or linked files.

driftCheck.title: Intent check after each turn
driftCheck.description: fork: after a turn that changed files, one tool-less question over the session asks whether the change still matches the user's words and the spec. off: deterministic checks only.

mapModel.title: Model for mapping and transcript-less checks
mapModel.description: The model that maps requirements to tasks (/xref map) and runs a drift check when there is no transcript to fork yet (an alias such as haiku, or a model id).

autopilot.title: Autopilot
autopilot.description: off: each Spec Kit step waits for you. on: every session starts with the autopilot switched on; after a turn it hands the next step to Claude by itself and stops only for decisions that are yours (/xref auto on|off switches it per session).

autopilotMaxSteps.title: Autopilot step budget
autopilotMaxSteps.description: How many steps one autopilot run takes before it waits for you.

review.title: Review gates
review.description: Where the autopilot stops until you approve (the pane, /xref approve or the dialog). spec+design: at the written spec, and at the design (DESIGN.md and the mocks) of a feature with a user interface. spec: only at the spec. spec+plan / spec+plan+design: also at the plan. none: no review, for maximum autonomy.

testCommand.title: Test command
testCommand.description: The command that runs the project's tests (e.g. npx vitest run). Empty: derived from plan.md's **Testing**: line. The autopilot runs it after each implement step; failures become repair steps, at most three.

junitPath.title: JUnit report
junitPath.description: Where the test command writes a JUnit XML report (e.g. reports/junit.xml). With it, each requirement is proven by the tests that name or anchor it; without it, a passing suite proves every requirement that has a real test.

commitPerTask.title: Commit per task
commitPerTask.description: on: after an autopilot step whose tests passed, the tasks it checked off are committed with their files (feature branches only, never main; nothing you staged is mixed in; files outside the plan or .env files stop it). off by default.

parallel.title: Parallel [P] tasks
parallel.description: on: a phase's open [P] tasks go to subagents of their own (speckit-xref:task-runner), one per task, and the main agent checks them off. off by default.

pane.title: Open the pane
pane.description: auto: the pane opens by itself where it is a sidebar (fullscreen). always: it opens with every session in a Spec Kit project (the terminal seats it from 144 columns, 110 once you have opened it; narrower, the band's Pane button opens it). off: only /xref pane opens it.

validate.title: Validate a new idea
validate.description: on: before a new project's first spec, the idea is researched on the web (who has the problem, what exists, what differs, the riskiest assumption) into .specify/memory/idea-brief.md, and you decide Build, Sharpen or Drop. The idea's wording goes to the web search Claude uses. off: straight to the spec.

shape.title: Shape the first version
shape.description: on: before a new project's first spec, Claude asks you what the idea leaves open (first-version scope, platforms, language, design, data) and records it in .specify/memory/product-brief.md, so the spec treats it as decided. off: the spec decides and calls it assumptions.

design.title: Design step
design.description: on: a feature with a user interface (plan.md's Project Type) gets its look after the plan and before the tasks: DESIGN.md at the root (Google Stitch's format) and a static HTML mock per screen in specs/<feature>/design/, shown on the dashboard. off: the tasks follow the plan directly.
